title: 1.4 Major Geological Processes
description: Endogenic and exogenic forces, folding, faulting, earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanism. Easy level.

questions.question: What are endogenic forces?
options: In Benioff zones along subducted plates
About 800 kilometers per hour
Forces that originate inside the Earth
Land between two faults that has sunk down
questions.correctAnswer: Forces that originate inside the Earth

questions.question: What are exogenic forces?
options: A fracture forms and one limb is pushed forward over the other
The bending of rock layers due to sideways earth movements
Shock waves released by shifting rock during an earthquake
Forces that originate outside Earth, mainly in the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: Forces that originate outside Earth, mainly in the atmosphere

questions.question: What is folding?
options: Forces that originate outside the Earth, mainly in the atmosphere
A fracture forms and one limb is pushed forward over the other
Shock waves released by shifting rock during an earthquake
The bending of rock layers due to sideways earth movements
questions.correctAnswer: The bending of rock layers due to sideways earth movements

questions.question: What is an upfold called?
options: Syncline
Anticline
Epicenter
About 80 percent

questions.question: What is a downfold called?
options: Syncline
Epicenter
Anticline
About 80 percent

questions.question: What is a fault?
options: The Appalachian Mountains
A crack in the Earth crust
More than 75 percent
About 800 kilometers per hour
questions.correctAnswer: A crack in the Earth crust

questions.question: What is a rift valley?
options: A giant ocean wave generated by underwater earthquakes
In Benioff zones along subducted plates
Land between two faults that has sunk down
Forces that originate inside the Earth
questions.correctAnswer: Land between two faults that has sunk down

questions.question: What is a block mountain also called?
options: Syncline
Anticline
Epicenter
Horst

questions.question: What is an earthquake?
options: Forces that originate outside the Earth, mainly in the atmosphere
A fracture forms and one limb is pushed forward over the other
The slow bending of rock layers caused by sideways earth movements
Sudden ground shaking caused by rock masses changing position
questions.correctAnswer: Sudden ground shaking caused by rock masses changing position

questions.question: What is the point on the surface directly above an earthquake focus called?
options: Syncline
Epicenter
Anticline
About 80 percent
